theorems.name: Theorem A (E_F and M_F false for A3)
theorems.statement: The system A3 over F_3 has negative drift (-1/3 per digit) and free re-entry. Its branches are f/t; (1+t^2)(f-1)/t when f(0)=1; (f-2)/t+1 when f(0)=2. Take L=2*3^k, X=3^{L+2} and h=log_3(2 sqrt 2). Then for every b, including b=infinity, N(X,b) >= (2 sqrt 2)^L/(L(L+1)) - 1 >= X^h/(9 log_3^2 X) - 1, while X P(b) <= X 3^{-(1-h)b}. So the count law fails for every K>1, and sigma(f)=infinity for polynomials of unbounded degree. The count law holds exactly inside the horizon.
theorems.novelty: new as far as checked; the explicit bound overtakes X P(2 log X) from L=486 on, and the enumeration shows the excess already at D=10

theorems.name: Theorem F (Frobenius cycles)
theorems.statement: Suppose a branch word w of digit length L has G_w = t^L + c with c a nonzero constant. Then -H_w/c is a polynomial periodic point lying in the cylinder of w, and these points are distinct for distinct words. Consequently #{f != 0 : deg f <= L+kappa, sigma(f)=infinity} >= |W_L|/L - 1, where W_L is the set of such words. For binomial systems (A3 with L=2*3^k, Q4b with L=3*2^k, S2c with L=2^k) W_L is the set of all zero-slope words of length L.

theorems.name: Theorem A' (Q4b, S2c)
theorems.statement: The same failure of E_F and M_F holds for Q4b over F_4 for every K>1, since the two exponents agree exactly: 4^h = 60.75^{1/3}. For S2c over F_2 it holds for K >= 1.05, from exact counts at L=2048. Extending S2c to all K>1 needs the standard method-of-types limit, which is quoted, not proved here.
theorems.status: PROVED (S2c for all K>1 uses a quoted standard result)

theorems.name: Lemma T and Corollaries T1, T2 (top-digit decoupling, cycle inequality, Frobenius sawtooth)
theorems.statement: Write T^n f = (G_w f + H_w)/t^L. Then deg H_w <= L + kappa + R, so the top digits of the orbit depend only on the branch counts. If f is periodic with deg f = D, then deg(t^L - G_w) <= L + kappa + R - D. When only one multiplier is non-constant, every cycle at degree D satisfies nu * p^{v_p(n_1)} >= D - kappa - R.
theorems.novelty: the function-field analogue of the integer cycle inequality |2^L-3^a| <= CL2^L/n

theorems.name: Horizon lemma
theorems.statement: N_D(b) = (q-1) q^D P(b) exactly whenever b + e_max - 1 <= D (and D >= D_0).

theorems.name: Corrected law (binomial systems)
theorems.statement: For all b >= log_q X, N(X,b) = X^{h+o(1)} along X = q^{L+kappa+1}: survivors stop thinning at the horizon.

theorems.name: Integer counterpart (Catalan words)
theorems.statement: Under 3x+d, parity words with 2^L - 3^a = +-1 give exactly the cycles {-1}, {1,2}, {-5,-7,-10} (times d). By Mihailescu's theorem (quoted) there are no others, so the Frobenius mechanism yields only finitely many integer exceptions.

theorems.name: Generic systems (B3, G3, S2, Q4)
theorems.statement: The count law holds within noise up to b of about 2D; after that cycles create an excess, with a deficit for Q4. Cycle counts grow in a sawtooth at powers of p. Heuristically about q^{p^k(hM - deg Delta)} Frobenius cycles exist, so E_F fails generically as well.

theorems.name: Possibly divergent orbits despite negative drift
theorems.statement: Orbits in A3, B3, G3, S2c and Q4b pass degree 4000 without repeating (for example the A3 orbit grows at about 0.33 degrees per step). No certificate was found.

prove:funcfield.blocking_points: For generic (non-binomial) systems the failure of E_F rests on numbers and a heuristic. What is missing is a proof that Delta^{p^k} divides H_w for exponentially many words whose branch counts are divisible by p^k. No positive theorem beyond the horizon was found for any polynomial system: the linear-algebra reformulation (equidistribution of H_w mod G_w) is as hard as E itself. The apparently divergent orbits with negative drift have no certificate; a line-renormalization search covered 12,446 of 927,866 candidate directions without success. The S2c case for all K>1, and the Baker and Mihailescu statements, are quoted rather than proved.
prove:funcfield.summary:
The function-field analogue of Conjecture E, and of its minimal form M, is false. I proved this for A3 over F_3, a system with negative drift and free re-entry, and also for Q4b over F_4 and S2c over F_2.

The mechanism is Frobenius. (1+t^2)^{3^k} = 1 + t^{2*3^k}, so for every zero-slope word w of length 2*3^k the periodic point -H_w/c is a polynomial. That gives at least X^h/(log X)^2 polynomials with sigma = infinity, while the Haar prediction X P(b) tends to 0. The count law therefore holds exactly up to the horizon and fails for every K>1. For binomial systems the corrected law is that survivors stop thinning at the horizon.

Lemma T shows the cause: without carries, the top digits evolve only through the branch counts, and Frobenius gives them near-returns. Its corollary deg(t^L - G_w) <= L + kappa + R - D is the analogue of the integer cycle inequality. In Z, Baker's theorem rules out near-returns and Mihailescu leaves exactly the cycles -1, {1,2}, {-5,-7,-10} (checked).

Lesson for the integer proof: an argument using only the digit, cylinder and affine structure would also prove E for A3, so a proof of E needs an archimedean input (Baker-type separation, or equidistribution of a log_2 3 mod 1) carried into the middle digits by carries.

Generic polynomial systems follow the Haar count to about twice the horizon and then break; this is evidence and a heuristic, not a proof. Orbits with negative drift that look divergent remain open.

theorems.name: Theorem R (reduction, uniform in the intercept)
theorems.statement: Setting: 3x+1 Terras map, coefficient stopping time tau; N(m,b) = #{n < 2^m : tau(n) > b}. For every m, j >= 1 and split depth j' with j <= j' <= m, put d = m - j' and K = j + j'. Then Sum_A Cnt_d(A) min_B Phi(3^A,B) <= N(m,m+j) <= Sum_A Cnt_d(A) max_B Phi(3^A,B), and Sum_A Cnt_d(A) Phi_bar = 2^m P(m+j). Here Phi(u,B) = #{s < 2^{j'} : u s + B mod 2^K in S_{d,A}}, S_{d,A} is the in-horizon survivor set, and B ranges over all of Z/2^K. Hence |N/2^mP(m+j) - 1| <= max_A r_A. No information about the intercept T^d(r), whose low bits are the beyond-horizon data, is used.
theorems.status: PROVED; checked against brute-force counts in 1369 cases (3x+1 up to n < 2^34; 3x-1 and 3x+5 up to n < 2^32; j <= 8)
theorems.novelty: New to the repo. The key point is bounding uniformly over the intercept B, which avoids the circularity of conditioning on B's middle bits.

theorems.name: Theorem C (certified beyond-horizon counts)
theorems.statement: For m = 100, 1000, 3000 and j = 1..12: N(2^m, m+j) = 2^m P(m+j)(1+delta), with |delta| <= 2e-5 (j = 1) up to 0.019 (j = 12); for example |delta| <= 0.0093 at m = 1000, j = 12. For every m in [35,1000] at j = 4: |delta| <= 0.0062. The in-horizon sandwich gives about [-0.97,+0.69] at j = 12.

theorems.name: Lemma F (averaged uniform discrepancy)
theorems.statement: For any S in Z/2^K, j' >= j = K - j' >= 1, and u uniform on a coset of <3> in (Z/2^K)^*: E_u max_B |Phi(u,B) - Phi_bar| <= g_K sqrt(|S|(1 - |S|/2^K)), with g_K = 4(1 + 0.3466(K-1)).
theorems.status: PROVED (Fourier, complete geometric sums over the cyclic group, Parseval); checked exactly in 432 cases, worst ratio 0.064
theorems.novelty: standard technique applied to the new problem

theorems.name: Theorem D (almost all octaves, log log X digits beyond the horizon)
theorems.statement: Fix eta > 0. For large M, all but at most M^{1-eta/3} of the m in [M,2M) satisfy |N(2^m,b) - 2^m P(b)| <= 2 m^{-eta/3} 2^m P(b) for every b with m < b <= m + (h0/2 - eta) log2 m, where h0 = 0.9430 is certified (h0/2 = 0.4715). Explicit finite form: the number of bad m is <= 2 n_s (lambda+3)(K+1) g_K 2^j M / (eps sqrt(#surv(K))). The same holds for every 3x+d with d odd.
theorems.status: PROVED (uses Lemmas F, P, M and elementary counting of the drifting window A ~ m lambda mod 2^{K-2}); the constants become effective only for M >= about 2^65

theorems.name: D' (explicit densities at K = 16)
theorems.statement: Weyl plus exact computation over all 2^14 multipliers and all 172 slot patterns. The upper density of the m with |N(2^m,m+1)/2^mP(m+1) - 1| > 0.05 is <= 0.002; at j = 2 and eps = 0.1 it is <= 0.002; at j = 4 and eps = 0.1 it is <= 0.136.

theorems.name: O1 (obstruction to route (i))
theorems.statement: Only A in [amin(d), amin(d+K)), a window of about 0.63K consecutive integers, matter, because A is fixed by the slope level. So a local limit theorem for A mod 2^{2j-2} among survivors cannot supply equidistribution of 3^A. The randomness has to come from the specific value of 3^A (Theorem C) or from the window drifting with m (Theorem D).

theorems.name: Generalisation to 3x+d
theorems.statement: Theorems R, C, D and D' hold for every odd d, with multiplier 3^A d^{-1}. This uses T_d(x) = d T_1(x/d) on Z_2. The extra cycles of 3x-1 and 3x+5 are tolerated.

prove:microrange.summary: For 3x+1 counted by the coefficient stopping time, I proved a reduction, Theorem R. It brackets N(2^m, m+j), the number of n < 2^m not dropped after m+j steps, between two sums that depend only on data mod 2^{m-j'} and on the multipliers 3^A mod 2^{j+j'}. The bracket holds uniformly over the unknown intercept T^d(r), whose low bits are exactly the beyond-horizon information, so there is no circularity. Evaluated exactly (Theorem C), it certifies the count law of Conjecture E beyond the horizon. Examples: within 0.93% at m = 1000, j = 12; within 0.62% for every m in [35,1000] at j = 4. The in-horizon sandwich only gives about +-50-90%. Combining a Fourier/Parseval averaged-discrepancy lemma (Lemma F) with Lemma P (patterns no harder than the root), Lemma M (supermultiplicativity, h0 = 0.943) and the drift of the window A ~ m log_3 2 gives Theorem D: for all but M^{1-eta/3} of the m in [M,2M), the count law holds with relative error 2m^{-eta/3} at every depth up to log2 X + (0.4715 - eta) log2 log2 X. Everything holds for every 3x+d with d odd, and agrees with brute force for 3x+1, 3x-1 and 3x+5. Route (i) as proposed fails, provably: A is pinned to a window of about 0.63K values by the slope level. The all-m version, larger depths and split5_3/K7 remain open; README.md in the folder records exactly where each one stalls.

theorems.name: F1 (exact Fourier identity)
theorems.statement: For X = k p^{b-m}: N(X,b) - X P(b) = p^{-b} sum over xi != 0 with v_p(xi) < m of S^(xi) conj(I_X^(xi)). Frequencies with v_p(xi) >= m are annihilated. Hence |N/(XP) - 1| <= B_F(b,m) = X^{-1} sum_{v_p(xi)<m} |mu_b^(xi)| |I_X^(xi)|.
theorems.novelty: standard Plancherel; the valuation restriction is the useful point

theorems.name: F2 (bounded distance past the horizon <=> pointwise Fourier decay)
theorems.statement: These are equivalent: (a) N(k p^{b-m}, b)/(k p^{b-m} P(b)) -> 1 for every fixed m, k; (b) mu_b -> Lebesgue weak-*; (c) mu_b^(xi) -> 0 for every fixed xi != 0.
theorems.novelty: standard equidistribution argument, applied to E

theorems.name: F3 (conditional: H => E up to 1/(1-h/2))
theorems.statement: If B_F(b,m) <= C p^m |R_b|^{-1/2+eps} (hypothesis H), then E holds for b <= log_p X / (1 - (1/2 - 2eps) h). That is 1.90 log X for 3x+1 and 1.41 log X for split5_3, short of C*.
theorems.status: PROVED (conditional); H is EVIDENCE: the ratio B_F/(2^m |R_b|^{-1/2}) is 1.3-1.9 for 3x+1, 2.5-3.3 for K7 and 3.3-4.2 for split5_3, b = 18..26

theorems.name: F4 (ceiling of the Fourier method)
theorems.statement: B_F(b,m) >= (2/pi)(1/(2 X P(b)) - 1) for all b, m. So no bound that puts absolute values on Fourier coefficients certifies anything once X P(b) < 1/(2+pi) = 0.194. In particular no such bound can give M or E_0.

theorems.name: Lemma T and Theorem U (transfer bound uniform in depth)
theorems.statement: Above an alive node r1 mod p^j, the surviving lifts t are exactly those with (U t + floor(x/p^s)) mod p^L in All(sigma, A), a finite set fixed by the state and the threshold. Consequently, for all b >= L: |mu_b^(xi)| <= kappa_{L, v_p(xi)} and |N(k p^{b-m}, b)/(X P(b)) - 1| <= D_{L,m,k}. Both bounds are computable from finitely many sets. For 3x+1, L = 22: D <= 0.1948, 0.4330, 0.8777 for m = 1, 2, 3, valid for every b >= 22.
theorems.status: PROVED (identity checked exactly; the numerical bounds use double-precision FFT, error far below the margins but not certified exactly)
theorems.novelty: new here. Weak: at fixed b the trivial sandwich gives bounds of the same size; useless for split5_3 (D = 3.5) and near-trivial for K7 (D = 0.999)

theorems.name: Proposition Z
theorems.statement: 3x+1: if no power of 3 lies in [2^{b-1}, 2^b), then R_b = R_b + 2^{b-1}, all odd-frequency coefficients vanish, and N(2^{b-1}, b) = |R_b|/2 exactly.

theorems.name: S (2-adic Syracuse form)
theorems.statement: 3x+1: r = -sum_k 3^{-k} 2^{e_k} mod 2^b for every r in R_b. So mu_b^ is the characteristic function of a 2-adic Syracuse variable conditioned on survival. It is exactly uniform without the conditioning.

theorems.name: G (gap in E => M)
theorems.statement: E with additive error X^{eps(X)} does not imply M. The corrected form E_0, with additive error eps(X) -> 0 beyond the finite set of exceptional starts, does imply M.

theorems.name: N2/N3 (non-decay of the top-level sup; its arithmetic structure)
theorems.statement: For 3x+1 the maximum of |mu_b^| over odd xi stays about 0.05 for b = 20..27 (random-set baseline 0.003-0.02). The maximisers are xi = +-2^v u^a with a near (b - v) log_u 2 - 1; at b = 27 the maximiser is exactly xi = 3^15. Low frequencies 1 <= xi <= 64 decay like |R_b|^{-1/2}.

prove:fourier.evidence: I computed the exact sets R_b with rb.c for split5_3, 3x+1 and K7 up to b = 30. FFTs at b = 24 to 28 are in spectrum_b24.txt, decay.txt, decay_c31_28.txt, profile_b26.txt and powers_b24.txt. The L1 criterion was tested on real data (l1test_b26.txt, l1_vs_b.txt). At b = 26 it certifies the 3x+1 count up to m = 9 digits past the horizon (B_F = 0.87) and fails from m = 10 on, which matches the 1/(1-h/2) ceiling. Theorem U numbers are in ub_*.txt. check_fourier.py runs exact checks [1]-[7] and exits 0. A mutation test showed it fails, with 2592 failures, when the transfer identity or the Syracuse identity is perturbed. The exact top-digit counts (topdigits.txt) deviate from the Haar prediction by less than 0.003, well inside the proved bound.
prove:fourier.blocking_points: E_bdd (mu_b^(xi) -> 0 for fixed xi) is open for every system. Theorem U loses the outer phases through the triangle inequality, so it is capped at kappa_L. Numerically kappa_L flattens at about 0.059 for 3x+1 (0.087, 0.074, 0.065, 0.059, 0.059 at L = 16..24), which matches the observed non-decaying sup. Getting cancellation over r1 needs the pairs (U(r1), floor(x/p^s)) mod p^L to be equidistributed over alive nodes, and that is E again: the argument is circular. Hypothesis H is supported only for b <= 26 and, even if true, reaches only 1/(1-h/2). F4 proves that absolute-value Fourier arguments can never reach M; a proof would have to use the signs of the coefficients. A Tao-type uniform-in-xi decay for the conditioned 2-adic Syracuse variable is numerically false because of the xi = +-2^v u^a spikes. All results use the slope-sense count, not the lead's actual-value count. G was not treated.
prove:fourier.summary: I put Conjecture E into Fourier form exactly. m digits past the horizon involve only the frequencies with v_p(xi) < m (F1). E at bounded distance past the horizon is equivalent to mu_b -> Lebesgue, i.e. to pointwise decay of mu_b^ (F2). A square-root L1 hypothesis H, numerically supported for the three systems, gives E up to b = log X/(1-h/2) (F3). F4 proves this method cannot certify anything once X P(b) < 0.194, so it can never give M. A transfer identity (Lemma T, checked exactly) gives Theorem U: finite computations at depth L bound the Fourier coefficients and the counts m digits past the horizon uniformly for every b >= L. For 3x+1 the error is within 19.5%, 43%, 88% for m = 1, 2, 3 and all b >= 22. This is valid but no better than trivial bounds at fixed b, and it is useless for split5_3. I also found that the lead's 'E => M' does not follow with the X^eps error term and gave a corrected form E_0. Numerically, the top-level coefficients do not decay. Their worst frequencies are exactly +-2^v u^a, which is the S-unit 'middle digits' structure, and it rules out Tao-type uniform decay statements. The literature survey (Tao, Sahlsten-Stevens, Bourgain-Dyatlov, Li, Shmerkin-Wu, Mahler/intrinsic approximation) explains why none applies; sources I checked online are labelled as checked, the rest as from memory. Everything is written up in README.md.
